note: Buy now, pay later lender (San Francisco). Ribbit's first documented round is Affirm's April 2019 Series F: its AF-F Ribbit Opportunity III vehicle (Form D, 2019Q2) and Ribbit Capital III both signed the amended investors' rights agreement filed with the S-1 (exhibit 4.2, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820953/000110465920126927/tm2026663d5_ex4-2.htm). Ribbit Capital III is a 2015 fund, so any earlier fund cheque falls in 2015 or later, when Affirm was past its Series A; the entry is Growth either way. Public since January 2021 (NASDAQ: AFRM); the market cap is pinned in the A/B pass.

Crypto exchange. Ribbit joined the $5M round of May 2013 led by Union Square Ventures (Global Venturing: USV 'led the round, and was joined by Ribbit Capital'), which Wikipedia names the Series A; it then joined the $25M round of December 2013 with Andreessen Horowitz and USV (Wikipedia) and, through its CB and CB-D vehicles, the 2015 Series C and the 2017 Series D. Ribbit held more than 5% before the listing (the 2020 DRS). Public since the April 2021 direct listing (NASDAQ: COIN); the market cap is pinned in the A/B pass. Remote-first since 2020, with a San Francisco office as its physical headquarters from 2025 (Wikipedia).

Blockchain-based lender (HELOCs on the Provenance chain). Principal office 100 West Liberty Street, Reno, Nevada (the 2025 S-1/A, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2064124/000162828025041731/figuretechnologysolutionsi.htm). Ribbit co-led, with DST, the company's first institutional round of May 2018, about $50M (FinTech Global; the Form D of 2018-05-24 sold $51.1M). The next round was the named $65M Series B of February 2019 (the company's release, Ribbit participating), and Wikipedia names a 2018 Series A, so the 2018 round is the Series A: the band's Growth reads the round size, not the round, and is disputed. Ribbit Capital IV held 10.9% before the IPO. Public on NASDAQ (FIGR) since September 2025; the market cap is pinned in the A/B pass.

Small-business lending marketplace (London). The known country US is a wrong join (the American subsidiary); Funding Circle is British, as the Accel and USV sibling rows also record. Ribbit joined the $37M round of October 2013 led by Accel with USV and Index (Wikipedia), which AltAssets names the Series C (https://www.altassets.net/private-equity-news/by-news-type/deal-news/accel-leads-37m-series-c-round-for-non-banking-loan-business-funding-circle.html); USV and Index had funded the A and B, so Ribbit's entry is Growth. Its FC and FC-GEM vehicles followed. Listed on the London Stock Exchange since September 2018 (FCH); the market cap is pinned in the A/B pass.

Indonesian retail brokerage and investment app, Jakarta (FX News Group). Ribbit led the $65M extension of Ajaib's Series A in March 2021, which followed a $25M first close in February (KrASIA: 'extended Series A round led by Ribbit Capital'); the October 2021 $153M Series B made Ajaib a unicorn (Jakarta Globe), the known $1B mark. SBI bought about 20% in August 2026 (FX News Group; $270M per the Forbes headline) with no valuation stated, so no new figure is minted here; the A/B pass should re-read the mark.

French health insurer (Paris). The known 'defunct' is a wrong join: Alan raised EUR 480M led by Prosus at a EUR 5.5B valuation in June 2026 (trendingtopics), the mark the Coatue sibling row also carries. EUR 5.50B @ ECB 2026-06-25 (EUR/USD 1.1342) = $6.24B. Ribbit was already an existing investor in the EUR 185M Series D of April 2021 led by Coatue (Orrick: 'historical investors Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital'; Partech's release, https://partechpartners.com/news/healthcare-super-app-alan-raises-185m-at-14bn-valuation-to-provide-personalised-healthcare-to-everyone-in-europe), and its AL-D vehicle bought into that round, but no source names the earlier round Ribbit entered: the Series C coverage of April 2020 (Temasek lead) does not list it, so the stage is undetermined.

The row is Offchain Labs, the company that builds Arbitrum (decisions.md D2); Ribbit bought equity in a priced round, so the stage is read normally and the row takes no token flag. Ribbit is named among the investors in Offchain's $120M Series B of 31 August 2021 at a $1.2B valuation, after the $20M Series A of April 2021 led by Lightspeed (cryptonews.net). No later equity round found (news sweep 2026-09-28), so the 2021 mark stands, stale, as on the Lightspeed sibling row. HQ New York, as that row.

Merchant payments and credit, New Delhi (Wikipedia; the Coatue sibling says New Delhi, the Insight sibling Gurugram). Ribbit co-led, with Steadview, the $50M round of August 2019 as a new investor; the $15.5M Series A of April 2019 had come from Insight, Sequoia and Beenext (Inc42), so Ribbit's first round is the Series B, a Growth entry. Its BP-E vehicle joined the $370M Series E led by Tiger Global at $2.85B in August 2021 (Moneycontrol).

Blockchain analytics and investigations, New York City (Wikipedia). Ribbit came in as a new investor, with Sound Ventures, in the $13M extension of the Series B in July 2020, joining previous investors Accel, Benchmark, MUFG and Sozo (FinTech Global); a Growth entry. Focus follows the sibling rows (Security). The known $4.2B mark is the 2021 round; the siblings carry the $8.6B Series F of May 2022, same band.

Payments processor, London (Wikipedia). Ribbit is named an existing investor in the $1B Series D of January 2022 at $40B (TechCrunch), but not among the investors of the June 2020 Series B (Coatue lead; Insight, DST, Blossom, GIC; the company's release) or the January 2021 Series C (Tiger lead; PYMNTS), and the $230M Series A of 2019 was the Insight and DST round: Ribbit's entry falls in 2021, after the Series C, a Growth position. Mark: the company's employee share buyback at $12B in September 2025 (TechCrunch, priced off a 409A), the figure the Coatue sibling row carries; the $40B of 2022 is the last primary round, same band.

Card acceptance and payments, Mexico City (the company's 2024 release). Ribbit's earliest vehicle in Clip is CL-C (Ribbit Opportunity IV, Form D 2020Q1, coded to the Series C); CL-D joined the $250M Series D of June 2021. No earlier Ribbit round was found: the May 2019 $100M round coverage names SoftBank and General Atlantic (LatamList), and the firm first listed Clip in 2022, when the company was past its Series D. The entry reads Growth.

Indian crypto investment platform, Bengaluru (Entrackr). Ribbit co-led, with Paradigm, the $15M Series A of January 2021, its first Indian crypto deal; Sequoia and Kunal Shah were existing investors (Entrackr). Mark: the $260M Series C led by Andreessen Horowitz and Coinbase at $1.9B (Reuters, 2021-10-06), aligned with the a16z sibling row; no later round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28, so the mark is stale.

Credit-card rewards and payments, Bengaluru (Wikipedia). Ribbit came in at founding: 'The company closed one of India's largest seed rounds at 30 million dollars from investors like Sequoia and Ribbit Capital' (Wikipedia), in 2018. The next round, $120M in August 2019 led by Ribbit, Gemini and Sequoia, is named (YourStory calls it the Series B, Moneycontrol the Series A), so the seed graduated. Meta's 20% stake for $900M in June 2026 (Wikipedia) prices the company at $4.5B, the figure the Coatue and General Catalyst siblings carry; the known $6.4B is the 2022 round, same band.

AI customer-service agents (San Francisco, as the siblings). That round made the company a unicorn (the company's release: 'Fenbeitong Hits Unicorn Status'); no figure was published, so the row carries the $1B floor, stale. The entry is Growth.

Balance (getbalance.com), B2B payments and net terms for merchants, with offices in New York and Tel Aviv (Calcalist); New York as the Lightspeed sibling. Stablecoin payments infrastructure (San Francisco). The known country GB is a wrong join, as the Sequoia sibling found. Streaming business-news network (New York). Altice USA bought Cheddar for $200M in cash, announced April 2019 and completed in June 2019 (AlleyWatch; Wikipedia), and sold it to Archetype in December 2023.

Cyber insurance, headquartered in San Francisco (the company's release). The band's Growth reads the 2022 Series F filing, a later round, and is disputed. The named $25M Series B of May 2019 (Crunchbase News) graduates the seed. Ribbit partner Nick Shalek sits on the board.

Philippine crypto exchange and e-wallet; CoinDesk calls it Manila-based, and it opened its office in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig, in 2023 (Newsbytes). Former Binance CFO Wei Zhou bought it from Gojek in April 2022 (CoinDesk); Ribbit then led the $30M Series C of May 2022 (the company's post), its first round here (the firm first listed Coins.ph in 2022): a Growth entry. Insurance and financial-product comparison for Chile, Colombia and Brazil, Santiago (the release dateline; the firm's archived label says Brazil, one of its markets). The site still serves Chile, Brazil and Colombia.

Cloud accounting and ERP for Brazilian small businesses (Joinville). Ribbit's Bets page already listed ContaAzul on 19 December 2012 (archive capture), before the 2013 filing the band anchors on, so the entry may be the September 2012 round ($2.76M Form D); a review of the entry date is suggested.

Digital bank for Brazilian small businesses, São Paulo (the company's site, https://www.cora.com.br/). The known country CA is a wrong join. Ribbit co-led, with Kaszek, Cora's first round, $10M, announced December 2019 (LatamList; the Form D sold $10.3M from 2019-09-13); the next round, the $26.7M of April 2021 that Ribbit led, is named the Series A (LatamList), so the first round is the seed and it graduated. The band's Growth reads the August 2021 Series B filing, a later round, and is disputed. Momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28. Consumer credit scores and financial-product marketplace. Blockchain and stablecoin developer platform (the founders are Spanish; the Form D gives an Orlando, Florida address).
